key_insight: The paper turns code judging from a binary verdict into an agentic verification task that also generates checkable counterexamples and failure diagnoses.
engineering_relevance: This matters for test-time scaling in competitive programming and code agents because better verification improves both candidate selection and iterative refinement under strict submission budgets.
method: Built USACO-JUDGE from USACO 2026 contest problems with accepted and unaccepted programs from human experts and multiple LLMs.
Trained ARBITER, a 35B MoE verifier, using reinforcement learning in a generic execution sandbox.
Used generated counterexamples as evidence to support verdicts and diagnosis.
evidence_signal: On USACO-JUDGE, ARBITER improved mean binary verdict accuracy from 71.41% to 87.41% and raised counterexample success on incorrect programs from 40.61% to 62.67%.
watch_item: The approach depends on sandboxed execution and generated counterexamples, so robustness may vary when programs are hard to trigger or when execution environments differ from official judges.
paper_title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
